SOURCE: board DM msg 658 (human:forrest, 2026-09-10T20:36Z): the long-term goal is a 'foreman of the factory' view of work in progress -- possibly anthropomorphic, 'full visualization, like a simulator video game' -- and the standing instruction is to put as much observability in place as possible. Filed by the CTO on the board member's behalf; the CTO's full reply is in the cto-owen/forrest DM (msgs 661 onward) and the AS-99 north-star comment.

WHAT IS MISSING (the gap this task closes): everything the company emits today is either STATE (advance.lock, deploy-state.json, git worktree list, .lattice task status, the roster) or COARSE EVENTS (Lattice status_changed / assignment_changed / branch_linked / comment_added at stage granularity). Nothing records the lifecycle of a LANE while it runs: when a tick started and ended and with what outcome; when a stage's sub-agent was spawned, for which task, as which employee, in which worktree; when it exited and whether it finished, errored, or was cut by the 30-minute tick timeout (AS-95's implementation stage was cut this way on 2026-09-10 and the only record is a board-commit message). Stage timers, per-lane liveness, and any future employee 'figure' state machine all need these events; none can be derived from the existing signals.

WHAT (v1, the plan refines): an append-only, typed, attributed JSONL stream of company events, written on the host by the tick and the watcher, read by the chat server, exposed as an API and pushed over the existing /api/stream. Event types, minimum set: tick_started {source, pid, nonce, startedAt}; tick_ended {outcome: ok|timeout|error|noop, lanesTouched[]}; stage_started {task, stage, actor, worktree, branch, ts}; stage_ended {task, stage, actor, outcome: completed|cut_by_timeout|error, ts}; subagent_spawned / subagent_exited {task, actor, stage, ts, exit}. Same envelope discipline as .lattice/events (schema_version, id, ts, actor, data) so a consumer that already parses Lattice events parses these. Producer: a tiny CLI in the mould of apps/chat/bin/chat.js (e.g. node apps/chat/bin/events.js emit stage_started --task AS-n --actor agent:x ...) that the orchestrator calls at stage boundaries -- the tick procedure already narrates every one of these in prose, so the change to .claude/commands/advance.md is one line per boundary (proposed wording goes in the plan for the metawork layer to apply; employees do not edit it). The watcher emits tick_started/tick_ended itself in fire()/settle(). Location: apps/chat/data/events/ (host-side, bind-mounted like deploy-state.json), gitignored like the rest of data/ unless the plan argues otherwise.

CONSUMER CONTRACT: the AS-99 lane projection (lanes[] with task, stage, employee, worktree, branch, ahead, dirty, lastCommit, stale) gains liveness fields (subagentAlive, stageStartedAt, stageElapsedS, lastEvent) from this stream with NO change to the lane card's shape. That is the acceptance test for 'extensible, not a one-off': AS-99's view consumes this feed by adding fields, not by rewriting.

DOCTRINE: one event stream, many projections -- the same rule as the derived org chart (AS-33) and the Lattice deep links (AS-93). Views never own state. Guards are proven by breaking them (M4): the plan names the falsifier for 'a stage cut by the tick timeout is recorded as cut_by_timeout, never as completed'.

EXPLICITLY NOT IN v1: tool-level activity of a running employee (reading a file, running tests) -- we do not own the harness and will not fake it; token/cost per stage (no source yet; note the slot in the schema); any spatial/animated rendering (that is the foreman floor, a later task over this stream); retention/compaction of the stream (append-only until it is a measured problem).

ORDERING: Chat set (tag chat, priority critical). Fourth, directly behind AS-99 -- CTO call under the board's delegation (DM msg 614); the metawork layer records the sentence in CLAUDE.md section Scheduling priority. Does not start before AS-95 lands: the lanes are only worth watching when they run unattended.
data.title: Chat: structured company-events feed — tick, stage, and sub-agent lifecycle events the UI can project (foreman-view substrate)

data.body: ORDERING (CTO call under the board's delegation, DM msg 614): fourth in the Chat set -- after AS-94 (needs_human, board bootstrap), AS-95 (in_progress, stays first), AS-99 (lane view; this task is the producer its second version consumes) -- and ahead of the age queue. Not started before AS-95 lands. Filed from board DM msg 658 (foreman-of-the-factory north star); the CTO's reply to the board is DM msg 661 (ack) and the substantive message that follows it. Planning owner: CTO (technical plan); the schema and the one-line-per-boundary change to the tick procedure are the two things the plan must settle, and the proposed advance.md wording goes in the plan file for the metawork layer to apply.

BOARD RULING (DM msg 668, human:forrest, 2026-09-11T01:56Z), answering the time-boxed question at the end of DM msg 663: "I think we'd want both. tool level activity can just be live as it happens, it does not need persistence"

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR AS-100: nothing in scope. This task remains the PERSISTED stream exactly as filed -- stage-level tick / stage / sub-agent lifecycle events, append-only JSONL, Lattice envelope. The EXPLICITLY NOT IN v1 line on tool-level activity still holds for THIS task; tool-level activity is now its own Chat-set task, AS-103, with a different storage rule.

THE TWO-SIGNAL RULE (binding on the AS-99, AS-100 and AS-103 planners):
1. STAGE-LEVEL STATE -- which employee is on which task at which stage in which worktree, since when; tick and sub-agent lifecycle -- is PERSISTED: written to the AS-100 JSONL stream on the host, readable after the fact, projected by the chat server. It is the sole source of truth for the foreman view's employee state machine (idle / planning / building / reviewing / waiting-on-board / blocked) and for stage timers.
2. TOOL-LEVEL ACTIVITY -- an employee reading a file, editing, running tests, waiting on docker -- is LIVE AND EPHEMERAL: it flows through a transient, in-memory channel only -- the chat server's existing SSE fan-out at /api/stream (server.js, the AS-25 streams Set), as a distinct event name (proposed event: activity), delivered to the connections open at that moment -- and is deliberately NOT written to the JSONL event stream, NOT written to the chat sqlite store, NOT written to any file under apps/chat/data/, .lattice/ or logs/, and NOT replayed to a client that connects later. A client that connects after a tool call learns nothing about it. The board's words are "does not need persistence"; I am tightening that to "must not be persisted" so a planner cannot read it as optional. Reason: a persisted tool-activity log would be a second event stream competing with this one under the one-stream-many-projections doctrine, at roughly 100x the volume, carrying payloads (commands, paths, contents) nobody decided to make a record.
3. THE FOREMAN VIEW COMPOSES THE TWO: the persisted signal decides which figure stands at which station in which state; the ephemeral signal animates the figure while frames arrive and decays back to the stage-level state after N seconds of silence. A page reload is truthful from signal 1 alone, and shows no history of signal 2.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS PLAN: the AS-100 plan names the /api/stream event names for BOTH signals (e.g. event: company for persisted AS-100 events, event: activity for AS-103's ephemeral frames) so a consumer subscribes to either without guessing, and states that only the former has an HTTP read-back endpoint. The persistence-boundary falsifier (M4) is AS-103's acceptance criterion, not this task's. Nothing else moves; ordering unchanged (fourth, behind AS-99, not before AS-95 lands).

PROPOSED CLAUDE.md WORDING (metawork layer applies; employees do not edit) -- append to the Observability north star paragraph: "Board ruling 2026-09-11 (DM msg 668): the foreman view carries both signals -- stage-level state is persisted (the AS-100 stream); tool-level activity of a running employee is live-only, pushed over the chat server's SSE channel and never written to any file or store (AS-103)."

What the cycle bought, and it is not nothing — a real finding about the test surface, found by writing the guard: serialiseEvent() returns the JSON WITHOUT a trailing newline (the producer adds it on append; api.test.js's eventLines() does the same by hand). My first draft appended lines without it. The server's tail only consumes up to the last 0x0a and holds the remainder as bytes, so all three tests saw ZERO company frames, and the tail's own state read reason:'ok', lastId:null — i.e. a stream that has planted events and reports itself healthy while delivering nothing. Discriminating probe that isolated it (four scratch node drivers, no source mutated): plant one event BEFORE construction and the tail's reason stays at its initial 'no-stream' rather than moving to 'ok' — proof the priming read consumed bytes but completed no line. Worth the reviewer's attention as an M6 lead: a producer that ever writes a partial final line leaves the tail silent and self-reported-healthy, which is exactly the failure the events feed exists to prevent. bin/events.js does append the newline, so this is a latent hazard, not a live defect.

After the newline fix: AC-13 (stream-company-change-only) PASSES — one append, one frame carrying that id; ten polls untouched, zero frames; two lines in one write, two frames in file order. Both need the next cycle.

Deviation to record now, because it is a plan/implementation mismatch a reviewer will hit: AC-14 says stream.reason==='truncated' appears on /api/events AND on the lanes projection's events. It cannot appear on /api/events as built — that endpoint re-reads the file through readStream(), and after a truncate the file it reads is intact; 'truncated' is a fact about THIS process's byte cursor, which only the tail (and therefore only the lanes projection's events block) holds. My draft asserts it on /api/lanes and asserts /api/events stays 200 with the post-truncate content. If the CTO wants the plan's literal wording, /api/events would have to report the tail's reason, which contradicts the cycle-3 decision that the two doors are deliberately separate readers.

Cycle 4, second half (developer-lena, 06:33Z) — what changed since my 06:29Z comment. Commit 281ebfc on feat/AS-100-events-feed: 'AS-100: cover change-only company frames and truncation (AC-13, AC-14)'. Worktree clean.

Root cause of the two remaining failures was NOT the server — it was my own drain helper. test/stream.test.js's openStream().nextFrame() pushes a waiter onto a queue and, on timeout, rejects WITHOUT removing that waiter. My first drain() was a loop of nextFrame() until the window expired, so every drain ended by leaving a dead waiter behind, and the next frame the server pushed was handed to it and dropped. That silently ate the first frame of the following window — which is exactly what 'two lines written, one frame seen' and 'no post-truncate frame' looked like. drain() now sleeps the window out and then takes what buffered (while (stream.pending()) nextFrame()), which never leaves a waiter, and carries a comment saying why. Flagging the underlying helper behaviour as an AS-25-era sharp edge for whoever touches this file next; I did not change the shared helper, because it is AS-25's and every existing test uses it correctly (they always have a frame coming).

Tests, host only, no docker: apps/chat suite 458 ran / 458 pass / 0 fail (branch was 456 at 1411753; +2 = the two committed tests). test/stream.test.js alone: 12 ran, 12 pass (baseline 10).

AC-13 (stream-company-change-only) and AC-14 (stream-company-truncation) are now on the branch and green — but note carefully: they are green tests, NOT yet met criteria under M4. Their named mutants (re-emit the last event each poll; throw on size < offset) have NOT been run, so no falsifier has been observed for either. Do not read 458/458 as AC-13/AC-14 satisfied.

AC-14 is written the way the CTO ruled at 06:30Z: 'truncated' asserted on the lanes projection's events block, /api/events asserted 200 with the post-truncate content.

AC-17 (stream-lanes-liveness-change-only) is NOT on the branch — it stays red and uncommitted in scratchpad/developer-lena/AS-100-cycle4-stream-tests.patch (228 lines, the three-test draft; apply to 1411753, then the AC-13/AC-14 halves are already merged at 281ebfc so cycle 5 should take only the AC-17 block from it). Its failure survived the drain fix: a single planted stage_started yields TWO lanes frames where the plan requires one.
